claims.statement: AgentKit owns the host-neutral agent loop, provider-facing runtime, approval handling, MCP and generic tool catalog, while Termind assembles host-specific SSH/SFTP tools, policy, persistence, and UI around it.

Accepted Termind submissions synchronously capture turn payload, context, model/provider/credential, permission and reasoning, search, skill/registry, Guardian and preparation settings before asynchronous compaction or memory loading; the controller assembles a fresh AgentRuntime and captured request without re-reading those mutable settings after the await. Exact AgentKit snapshot ordering relative to model and tool work is not established by this checkout.

ConversationModel keeps a display projection separate from the authoritative transcript because replaying display messages would lose tool calls and results; it owns the active runtime and consumes its ordered event stream.

Tool calls are schema-validated before approval and execution; Deny always refuses, Approve needs no further approval, and Ask follows permission mode, while full access does not bypass trust, secret, schema, sandbox, or capability boundaries.

Guardian review is used only for approve-for-me runs when a configured reviewer credential is available; unavailable, timed-out, malformed, or otherwise failed review denies execution rather than allowing it.

Secret handles are single-use and bound to run, tool, host, and purpose; secret values and handles are removed from replay and durable history rather than exposed to the model, review, events, logs, SwiftData, or Hermes memory.

ConversationModel queues steering to the active runtime without immediately appending it to transcript; a steeringDelivered event projects it to history, and runtime integration tests show it in the next model request and saved snapshot. Stop requests runtime cancellation, interrupts live cards and returns undelivered steering to the composer; the integration test observes tool cancellation but not precise secret-disposal timing.

Each tool-capable conversation receives a persistent, per-conversation scratch workspace that is isolated from other conversations; scratch paths reject escape and symlink routes, and scratch push rechecks the approved file digest before writing remotely.

SwiftData persistence stores conversation/run history and durable tool lifecycle records, deduplicates replayed messages by message ID, marks nonterminal runs interrupted on repository initialization, and restores recorded tool results to repair otherwise unanswered historical calls.

Compaction persists a record before the live conversation applies it and replaces only the model-facing projection with a synthetic summary; the original display history remains available after restore.

Skills are app-managed packages whose enabled catalog and inventory are captured at submission before preparation; only SKILL.md is procedural instruction, and a skill does not authorize commands, writes, or transfers outside the normal approval policy.

Hermes memory is device-local and disabled by default; its lazy GRDB store maintains memory state, review/learning checkpoints and a redacted FTS5 conversation-history index separate from authoritative SwiftData history, while migration removes the legacy per-conversation snapshots table.

Disabling Hermes memory invalidates contexts and cancels indexing/reviews while retaining storage; destroy persists disabled state, joins work and removes the owned directory. Generation checks reject stale access and UI publication, without rolling back a storage write already committed in flight.

Termind's static host-tool registrations are shared across Assistant surfaces; injected workspace capability controls scratch transfer construction, and AssistantToolRegistry returns no tools for models without toolCall rather than using a surface-registration flag.

Termind planning excludes remote SFTP mutations and scratch_push and reviewing receives no Termind tools; planning and acting share the ssh_exec schema while destructive-command preflight denies in planning and asks in acting, and proven-safe reads approve in parallel.

The terminal_suggest schema remains registered across Assistant surfaces, while its execution gate is captured in toolAvailability: TFM Workspace sidebar sends true, TFM standalone and TFI send false; this partial gate does not disable independent SSH/SFTP execution.

Conversation steering changes the sending session and only the terminal_suggest availability key, preserves other overrides and skill/plan/memory context, leaves a legacy absent snapshot unknown, and updates activeContextSnapshot only when delivery occurs.

Host discovery and SSH/SFTP work require no sidebar session or PTY; list_hosts exposes enabled protocols without credentials, including Telnet-only hosts, while SSH operations independently require SSH capability.

Historical tool cards resolve persisted presenter IDs through the immutable combined presenter registry or a closed legacy tool-name list; the terminal_suggest context key and presenter identities are independent of surface-registration arguments.

Desktop MCP server selects acting definitions then applies exported-name and disabled-tool filtering, exposing the allowed host tools, request_user_secret and four HTTP transfer tools rather than terminal, scratch, web, skill, plan or task tools; the stdio bridge forwards to that server. MobileAppModel contains no local MCP-server setup.

Desktop sidebar, standalone and mobile first sends use controller capture before library promotion; refused sends do not promote or consume drafts, while accepted composer/text sends fold attachments and armed skills once and direct text sends preserve unrelated draft text.

Desktop and mobile prepare edits synchronously before creating a UI task, preserving original attachment payload/suffix but capturing fresh submission context; performAgentEdit checks identity before tracked persistence and again before runtime preparation, and failed persistence does not apply the live edit.

Preparation is separate from streaming, with combined activity guards; stop, global cancellation and mobile background expiration synchronously invalidate preparation identity, cancel and join tracked history/preparation work, and recheck identity after the interrupted save so stale work cannot retire a newer capture.

Archive/delete cancel and join pending preparation before their activity guards; manual compaction refuses preparation, navigation leaves it active, and automatic compaction uses captured preparation settings while preserving persistence-before-live-apply ordering.

ConversationModel owns a queued runtime before starting its event consumer; stopping while queued constructs a cancelled snapshot from the captured request, saves it in a separate task, and stopAndWait joins that save via the consumer, without needing a running snapshot or model call. Presentation can cancel before save completes and queued-save errors are swallowed.

Implementing a pending plan captures a new acting submission with planContract cleared before resolving the plan, folds composer attachments and armed skill once, and leaves the pending plan and composer payloads untouched when refused.

Explicit startAgentRun reuses the last user turn's stored context snapshot or a neutral unknown legacy snapshot and captures current runtime configuration rather than replaying historical credentials or skill-package bytes; restored nonterminal runs become interrupted rather than automatically rerunning, and any provider-level retry belongs to the pinned AgentKit package.
A missing model or credential at capture stays a failed submission even if configuration is supplied during preparation.

New submissions capture memory-session eligibility before preparation; enabling later does not add a session, while disabling revokes existing contexts and rejects late snapshot loads from the prior generation, so captured eligibility does not ensure availability.

Automatic titles require a real nonempty authoritative transcript reply even if the run later stops and resolve title configuration live; non-planning runs with a valid memory learning token record activity, completed runs contribute user IDs, and review is gated on accumulated activity or an explicit force.

A validated history edit commits before live mutation and truncates from the selected ordinary user message in canonical run/message order, preserving a same-run prefix and its owned tool graph with a neutral completed summary while deleting wholly later runs, including empty runs; editing is rejected if any removed suffix has transcript tool activity or a durable tool invocation, even if only proposed, denied or read-only.

Edit tool cleanup prioritizes known source/call ownership; restore infers legacy source IDs and assigns recovered result ownership, letting live edits use retained result and full display-prefix ownership through compaction. Only unrecoverable ownership falls back to the inclusive timestamp cutoff, including modern provider-native events persisted before their source-message snapshot; compactions prune explicit removed boundaries, nil bases survive, and retained openings preserve the title.

A replacement message initially owns a same-ID completed staging run; the first real snapshot with that staged final user message transactionally reassigns only its row and sequence, retains attachments/replay backing, deletes staging and leaves historical replay owners unchanged. Staging orders after retained runs and supplies a start-time lower bound preserved on subsequent saves and terminal timestamps.

Live run-started, successfully saved captured-failure and preparation-interrupted paths adopt a staged edit's real run provenance and chronology; queued prestart cancellation also projects adoption. Preparation interruption saves before adoption and checks identity, while captured missing-model/credential failure keeps preparation owned until its save finishes, adopting only on success and leaving staging intact on failure.

Repository-instance retired IDs block late saves and tool events from edited target, removed later and adopted staging runs; truncation and snapshot-save errors roll back SwiftData changes and restore the previous retired-ID set.

Submitted turns separate authoredText for display/editing from model-facing text containing attachment blocks and an armed skill directive; structured images and context attachments accompany the request, and pendingPriorMessages omits the last user turn because its prompt is passed separately, as verified in an integrated saved-run test.

ConversationModel serializes user-input requests by creation time, starts a request's timeout only while it is the visible head, and clears drafts on cancellation or timeout; changing question steps does not reset that deadline.

AgentKit user-input tools accept an optional 1–1800 second timeout defaulting to five minutes and validate at most three questions; Termind requires each question to be answered or explicitly skipped to advance, does not allow skipping secrets, and keeps secret answers in a separate cleared draft.

Skipping a user-input question omits it from the interaction response but the model-facing request_user_input result reports the question with a null answer; cancelling or timing out returns a distinct outcome without partial answers.

ConversationModel queues manual approvals by creation time and only accepts an answer for the head; direct approval stages a tool card before channel events drain, and late approval notifications do not overwrite terminal denials.

Live approval presentation uses unredacted in-memory arguments for the user to review without appending that projection to durable cards or model transcript; normal tool detail presentation instead projects structured built-in JSON through presenters with a generic fallback, while MCP output retains its remote JSON form.

Tool presentation groups summaries by qualified tool, terminal state and knowledge action so mixed failures are not shown as successes, and bounds displayed output previews to 8192 characters and 120 lines while preserving full transformed output for copying.

Mobile app backgrounding suspends Hermes memory, and background expiration separately cancels pending Assistant preparations and active runs before draining run work and closing host connections; desktop termination also suspends Hermes memory.

Suspending Hermes memory revokes existing sessions and access without deleting stored memory; resume reloads state and schedules history indexing, but an old access handle remains invalid even after resume.

Termind declares a remote AgentKit version requirement starting at 0.18.1 and builds the committed resolved package rather than the sibling checkout; cross-runtime changes require an AgentKit release followed by the Termind package requirement and resolution update.

Termind's host-keyed AgentConnectionPool reuses a multiplexed SSH connection for exec and primary SFTP across runs and conversations, invalidates it when the route changes, and closes idle or explicitly disconnected connections rather than closing them at every turn.

AgentSSHAuthenticationRegistry shares temporary authentication only across overlapping attempts for a host, discarding the context after the last lease; SFTP authentication and lease acquisition can retry but the SFTP operation itself is executed once and released on success or failure.

Termind's ssh_exec retries a dead pooled connection only before a command session opens; on deadline expiry it distinguishes a still-connecting command that never ran from an already running command handed to the background command service for later ssh_wait.

Per-conversation chat-model selection is persisted before submission capture; drafts are seeded in memory, restored selections are backfilled and valid choices do not track later Chat-role changes, while a model selection save failure refuses the send before it consumes the draft.

If a captured missing-model or credential failure is already saving, stop, global cancellation, archive and delete join its in-flight failed snapshot save rather than writing an interrupted snapshot; failed-run presentation and staged-edit adoption occur only on save success, and a failed save shows an error and retires preparation without claiming a durable failed run.

Memory-session loading checks eligibility before preparing storage and rechecks its generation after the await before granting revocable context and access, so disabling during preparation can reject an already captured session without retaining old frozen per-conversation prompt snapshots.

Both native app adapters inject a shared AssistantChatCoordinator and captured source context into AgentKit's generic chat tool configuration rather than registering separate platform-specific collaboration tools; models without toolCall receive an empty registry.
The chat model catalog exposes enabled Chat models and their capability/readiness information while keeping credential values out of the catalog response.

Chat creation inherits the captured source's plan posture and permission mode and uses an explicitly available Chat model or the captured source model, but does not copy source composer, session context, attachments or armed skill into the new target; creation records provenance independently of later deliveries.

Cross-chat sending refuses self, archived or history-changing targets and prevents planning sends to an effectively acting target; an idle target captures its own settings without consuming the human composer, while a streaming target queues origin-tagged steering and returns undelivered agent messages without adding them to the human draft.

Cross-chat delivery receipts deduplicate retries by source run and tool call, keep delivered state monotonic, and persist the origin-tagged idle/new-chat prompt before accepting delivery; SwiftData commits the queued-to-delivered receipt transition with the origin message save across separate model contexts, while a failed prompt save cancels preparation and marks delivery undelivered and a later metadata failure does not revoke acceptance.

The coordinator reconciles queued cross-chat receipts on restore using the target's durable prompt, marks abandoned queued deliveries undelivered when no live owner survives, and returns the historical receipt on a retry after target deletion without recreating the target.

Chat listing pages visible conversations with batch-loaded creation relations that retain the original creator independently of later messages; reading returns bounded display history rather than full model replay, and chat waiting observes readiness only after preparation ends and races timeout or user interjection without stopping the target.
